title: INSPIRE: Accelerating Deep Neural Networks via Hardware-friendly Index-Pair Encoding
problem: Variable-length quantization for DNNs introduces significant hardware overhead in encoding/decoding, and existing quantization methods are less effective for both activations and weights due to the presence of outliers.
motivation: DNN inference consumes significant computing resources and memory, necessitating efficient acceleration techniques.
method: INSPIRE uses index-pair encoding, a method where values are stored with different amounts of precision depending on how unusual they are. Outlier values—ones that fall far outside the normal range—are stored with high precision, while typical values use lower precision to save space. The method uses index pairs to efficiently map between the original values and their compressed representations, which cuts down the computational cost of encoding (compressing) and decoding (decompressing) the data. It works for both neural network activations (the outputs of neurons) and weight values (the learned parameters).
key_novelty: Index-pair encoding that reduces the computational overhead of compressing and decompressing neural network values by automatically assigning high precision to outliers and low precision to normal values.
contributions: Index-pair encoding scheme for variable-length quantization with reduced hardware overhead
Unified quantization approach for both activations and weights
Hardware-optimized implementation for accelerated DNN inference
Improved handling of outlier values in neural networks
limitations: Limitations not discussed in the abstract.
